content.stem: When the polynomial \(2x^3 + ax^2 - 5x + 7\) is divided by \((x + 2)\), the remainder is \(-7\). Find the value of \(a\).

hints: By the remainder theorem, the remainder on dividing \(f(x)\) by \((x + 2)\) is \(f(-2)\).

steps.title: Use the remainder theorem
steps.explanation: Dividing by \((x + 2)\) means substituting \(x = -2\), the value that makes \(x + 2 = 0\).
steps.rule: Remainder theorem: when \(f(x)\) is divided by \((x - k)\), the remainder is \(f(k)\).

commonMistakes: Setting \(f(-2) = 0\) as if \((x + 2)\) were a factor, giving \(a = -\tfrac{1}{4}\).

alternativeMethods.title: Long or synthetic division
alternativeMethods.description: Dividing by \((x + 2)\) gives the remainder \(4a + 1\); setting it equal to \(-7\) gives the same result. This is longer than the remainder theorem.

criteria.description: Uses the remainder theorem with x = −2

questions.authorNotes: As a numerical question it is marked by the key alone; the rubric is for teacher reference.

hints: If \((x - 2)\) is a factor of \(f(x)\), then \(f(2) = 0\).
After finding \(k\), divide by \((x - 2)\) to get a quadratic, then factorise that quadratic.

steps.title: Apply the factor theorem
steps.rule: Factor theorem: \((x - a)\) is a factor of \(f(x)\) if and only if \(f(a) = 0\).

steps.title: Find k
steps.explanation: Solve for \(k\). The polynomial is now \(2x^3 + x^2 - 13x + 6\).

steps.title: Divide by the known factor
steps.explanation: By long division (or synthetic division with 2: coefficients \(2,\ 1,\ -13,\ 6 \to 2,\ 5,\ -3\), remainder 0) the quotient is \(2x^2 + 5x - 3\).

steps.title: Factorise the quadratic
steps.explanation: Find two numbers with product \(2 \times (-3) = -6\) and sum \(5\): these are \(6\) and \(-1\).

steps.title: Complete factorisation
steps.explanation: Check: the zeros \(2,\ \tfrac{1}{2}\) and \(-3\) each make the polynomial equal to zero.

commonMistakes: Substituting \(x = -2\) instead of \(x = 2\), which gives \(4k + 16 = 0\) and \(k = -4\).
Stopping at \((x - 2)(2x^2 + 5x - 3)\) without factorising the quadratic, so the factorisation is not complete.
Writing the factor for the zero \(\tfrac{1}{2}\) as \((x - \tfrac{1}{2})\) and losing the factor 2 (the product is then \(x^3 + \ldots\), not \(2x^3 + \ldots\)).

alternativeMethods.title: Comparing coefficients
alternativeMethods.description: Write \(2x^3 + x^2 - 13x + 6 = (x - 2)(2x^2 + px + q)\). Comparing the constant terms gives \(-2q = 6\), so \(q = -3\); comparing the \(x^2\) terms gives \(p - 4 = 1\), so \(p = 5\).

criteria.expectedEvidence: 2x² + 5x − 3, by long division, synthetic division or comparing coefficients
acceptedAlternatives: Finding another zero by trial (e.g. f(−3) = 0) and dividing accordingly
criteria.partialCreditRules: Follow-through if k is wrong but the division is carried out correctly for the student's polynomial.

questions.authorNotes: Zeros 2, 1/2, −3 verified by substitution; expansion of (x − 2)(2x − 1)(x + 3) checked.
